items.title: Pay Abschlag to 'new' bank account (LIKELY SCAM - do not pay without verification)
items.quote: Bitte überweisen Sie den fälligen Abschlag von 214,00 € bis spätestens 11.09.2026.
items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar due date, '11.09.2026', with no period to calculate. Today is 2026-09-08 (Tuesday), so the stated date simply stands as printed; no weekend/holiday adjustment is needed since 11.09.2026 is a Friday, a regular business day in NW.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a phishing/fraud scam: an abrupt 'change of bank details' combined with an urgent payment demand and a threat of immediate service disconnection 'ohne weitere Ankündigung' (without further notice) is a classic scam pattern, not normal utility practice.

The new IBAN's stated account holder, 'Global Energy Payments s.r.o.', is a foreign private company (s.r.o. = Czech/Slovak legal form) with no apparent relation to the German municipal utility 'Stadtwerke Musterstadt' — this mismatch is a major red flag and the payment should NOT be made to this account.

The sender's email domain 'kundenservice-mail.example' does not look like an official Stadtwerke domain, and the given contact is only a mobile phone number ('Sondernummer'), not a normal landline customer-service number.

The letter explicitly instructs the recipient not to reply in writing and to call only a specific phone number instead — a manipulative tactic commonly used in scams to prevent verification through official channels.

Do not use the IBAN or phone number given in this letter; instead verify this 'bank change' notice directly via the phone number or address on a previous, trusted bill or contract from Stadtwerke Musterstadt before paying anything or before assuming any real risk of disconnection.

Genuine German utility providers do not change their bank account to a foreign account controlled by an unrelated private company, nor do they demand payment within days under threat of disconnection without prior dunning procedure; this letter should be treated as fraudulent unless independently confirmed.
